thesis: The AI in this plan isn't mainly there to find rare earths in coal waste. A second AI is there to keep living microbes working as power rises and falls, so Alaska's hardest input, energy, is the design brief and not an afterthought.
falsifier: If the 2030 results show the bioreactor controller ignores available energy, or the energy and cost evaluation is a footnote, the thesis is false. No results exist yet.
supporting_facts: c6 a second AI effort will adjust the bioreactor as conditions and available energy change
c7 the refinery is tested first as a virtual pilot plant, computer models
c11 Aggarwal: Alaska's remote energy challenges make energy use central
counterpoint: Nothing has been tested (c9), no Alaska coal source is named, UAF is one of four partners with about $913,000 of roughly $6M, and a controller can adapt to costly power but can't make power cheaper. The old answer, ship ash where power is cheap, still has to be beaten.
runner_ups: Planned-not-proven skeptic reading (valence curious): true but the same facts, folded in as the Act 3 test.
Waste-as-feedstock comedy: kept as a sight-gag source.
second_movement: UAF joins, not leads: a seat at a national table, and the virtual plant is only models.
